You are ONE OF FOUR independent reviewers of a pull request. Work alone; do not assume another reviewer covers anything.

REPO: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa

=== ACCESS RULES (STRICT) ===
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, commit, push, or post anything to GitHub.
- DO NOT check out any branch. The working tree holds unrelated uncommitted work.
- The PR is fetched as the local ref `pr/61`. Read files with `git show pr/61:<path>`.
- Base (merge-base with develop) is `8362b3c`. Read base files with `git show 8362b3c:<path>`.
- Diff with `git diff 8362b3c pr/61 [-- <path>]`.
- DO NOT re-run any gate (no npm test/lint/build/tsc/playwright). Gates were already measured; numbers below. Your budget goes to what gates CANNOT see.

=== THE PR ===
#61 "SFCC-751: BrowserStack/Zephyr Scale QA automation pipeline", author TimLavelleACC,
`feature/browserstack-ci-automation` -> `develop`. 42 files, +2886/-266, 20 commits. Head 74e2b82.
CodeRabbit approved after several CHANGES_REQUESTED rounds; no human review yet.

=== JIRA TICKET SFCC-751 — VERBATIM, AS WRITTEN ===
Title: SFCC-751: QA Pipeline — Playwright spec generation, BrowserStack execution, and Zephyr Scale result sync

Overview
Implement the end-to-end QA pipeline that closes the loop between Zephyr Scale test cases and BrowserStack Automate execution results. This story covers three discrete deliverables that must be in place for the AI-assisted QA methodology to function as designed.

Background
Zephyr test case SFCC-T150 has been created and linked to SFCC-420. The pipeline requires:
- A Playwright spec tagged with the Zephyr test case key so BrowserStack knows what it is executing
- A GitHub Actions workflow that fetches BrowserStack results and posts execution records back to Zephyr Scale via the EU regional API
- A validated end-to-end run confirming the full chain works

Deliverables
Deliverable 1 — Playwright spec (SFCC-T150)
- Generate e2e/tests/zimm/integrations/SFCC-420-global-e-job-site-assignments.p1.spec.ts
- Spec must be tagged with Zephyr test case key SFCC-T150
- Scenarios must cover all 6 BDD scenarios in SFCC-T150
- Selectors via POM only — no inline selectors
- Tagged @SFCC-420 @global-e @integration @p1

Deliverable 2 — GitHub Actions sync script
- New workflow: .github/workflows/zephyr-results-sync.yml
- Triggers on completion of BrowserStack Automate run in CI
- Fetches BrowserStack session results via BrowserStack REST API
- Maps BrowserStack pass/fail to Zephyr test case key via spec tag
- Posts execution record to Zephyr Scale EU endpoint: https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2/testexecutions
- Attaches BrowserStack session URL and HAR to Zephyr execution record
- Zephyr API token stored as GitHub Actions secret: ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN
- BrowserStack credentials stored as: BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME, BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY

Deliverable 3 — End-to-end validation
- Trigger a BrowserStack run against the new spec
- Confirm execution record appears in Zephyr under SFCC-T150
- Confirm BrowserStack session URL is attached to the Zephyr execution record
- Document any manual steps required for ongoing operation

Acceptance Criteria
- Given a merged Playwright spec tagged with a Zephyr test case key, when BrowserStack Automate completes a run in CI, then an execution record is created in Zephyr Scale under the correct test case with pass/fail status and BrowserStack session URL attached
- Given the sync script runs, when it calls the Zephyr API, then it uses the EU regional endpoint https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2 and not the US default
- Given a BrowserStack run fails, when the sync script posts to Zephyr, then the execution record status is Failed and the BrowserStack session URL for debugging is included
- Given the pipeline runs end-to-end, when reviewed in Zephyr Scale, then SFCC-T150 shows an execution record linked to the BrowserStack run with correct status

Design/Technical Notes
- Zephyr Scale instance is on EU/DE regional API: https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2
- Do NOT use the US default endpoint https://api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2 — returns unknown token errors
- BrowserStack Automate REST API
- Zephyr Scale test executions API: POST /testexecutions with testCaseKey, testCycleKey, statusName, comment
- The .browserstack.yml is already scoped to e2e/tests/zimm — new spec picked up automatically
- Playwright spec naming convention: {JIRA-KEY}-{description}.{priority}.spec.ts
=== END VERBATIM TICKET ===

=== ALREADY-MEASURED GATE RESULTS (do not re-run) ===
PR touches ZERO files under `overrides/`. Gate coverage of the 42 changed files: lint 0/42 (not in qa.yml), audit:tokens 0/42 (not in CI; exits 1 at healthy baseline, 14 known pre-existing), tsc 1/42, Vitest 0/42 changed (job PASSED only because detect-changes watches vitest.config.*), Storybook 0/42 changed (PASSED only because package.json/lock changed), Playwright E2E localhost SKIPPING, BrowserStack E2E SKIPPING, Deploy Preview PASSED, File Tier & Squad Boundary PASSED.
`test:max-file-size` exits 1 on a healthy tree and is not in CI. `test:contracts` is a permanent `echo && exit 0` stub. A SKIPPED required check counts as PASSING on the merge button here.
=> Do NOT read these exits or green checks as evidence about this PR.

=== RUBRIC SOURCE (critical for your angle) ===
Read ALL house rules at BASE `8362b3c`, NOT head. This PR edits `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/testing.md` — two of the files it would be judged against. Judging it against its own edited rules is circular. Rule-file edits are reviewed separately, as changes.
Rubric files: AGENTS.md (Hard Rules), .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md (Tier 1), .claude/rules/protectedFiles.md (Tier 2), .claude/rules/conventions.md, .claude/rules/testing.md, CODEOWNERS.

=== ALREADY SETTLED BY THE LEAD — do not re-litigate ===
The `.browserstack.yml` -> `browserstack.yml` rename did NOT drop Tier 1 status: at head `frozenFiles.md:114` re-lists the un-dotted path with rationale and `CODEOWNERS:60` routes it to tier-1-approvers. (Still fair game: `protected-file-guard.yml` has no browserstack entry at base OR head.)

=== YOUR ANGLE: R2 — CONVENTIONS, TIER & OWNERSHIP ===
1. Classify all 42 changed paths by tier and owner per the BASE rubric. Where a path has no tier and no CODEOWNERS entry, say so — an unowned path is itself a finding worth stating.
2. Adjudicate against AGENTS.md Hard Rules. Known starting points (verify each yourself, and find the ones I have not listed):
   - Hard Rule 8: "Never modify test configuration files (vitest.config.*, playwright.config.*, .storybook/, tests/lighthouserc.js)". `vitest.config.ts` is modified (+18). Is `playwright.config.js` or `.storybook/` also touched? What exactly changed and does any stated justification exist in the PR?
   - Hard Rule 7: "Never add or remove packages from package.json without integration team approval." `@vitest/coverage-v8` ^3.2.7 added to devDependencies. Is there any evidence of approval in the PR body, commits, or comments?
   - Hard Rule 2/4: 12 Tier 1 paths are touched. Rule 4 names an ABSOLUTE set (ssr.js, config/default.js, config/sites.js, worker/main.js) where no exception applies — are any touched?
   - Hard Rule 10: "Never touch more than one protection tier in a single change without stopping to confirm scope."
   - Hard Rule 14: sprint-scope. Check .docs/memory/sprintScope.md.
3. `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-claude-code-brief.md` and `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md` (+418 lines combined) are the author's own AI working docs, committed as TRACKED files (`.docs/temp/` is not gitignored at base; the PR's .gitignore change is unrelated — it adds `test-results.json`). Should these ship? Check whether any precedent exists in repo history for committing `.docs/temp/` working files.
4. Derived-config mirror integrity: the PR changes both `.claude/rules/testing.md` AND `.cursor/rules/testing.mdc` (plus `.cursor/rules/skills/*.mdc`, `.cursor/rules/tier1FrozenFiles.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.vscode/instructions/workflows.md`). Per `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` and `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`, `.claude/` is the SOURCE and the rest are GENERATED. Verify the generated files are actually regenerated output and not hand-edited — i.e. does the .mdc content faithfully derive from the .md source, or has it drifted? This is checkable: read both and compare.
5. E2E file conventions per `.claude/rules/testing.md` at BASE and `e2e/features/README.md`: spec filename convention, required test tags (@area + @SFCC-NNN), Gherkin-first workflow (does a .feature exist for each spec, and was it Lead-QA-approved?), POM selector priority (accessible > semantic > test-id; never tag/class/DOM-position). Audit the new page objects in `e2e/support/pages/` against that priority order.
6. Naming/structure conventions from `.claude/rules/conventions.md` for the new scripts.

=== CONSTRAINTS ON YOUR OUTPUT (all mandatory) ===
- FALSIFY, do not confirm. Attack each claim the PR makes about itself, including claims in its own source comments and in the rule-file edits.
- Cite `file:line` for every finding.
- Label each finding CONFIRMED (proved) or PLAUSIBLE (reasoned but unproven).
- Severity: BLOCKER, DEFECT, or NOTE.
- When a count moves, prove WHICH items moved, not just how many. Enumerate identity where the set is small enough.
- For any check whose pass you rely on, try to make it pass WRONGLY — construct a decoy that should fail and reason through whether it would.
- Any "X exists nowhere" claim MUST state its search scope in the same sentence.
- Separate author-introduced from pre-existing. Pre-existing -> NOTE unless the PR's own premise makes it a defect.
- MANDATORY CLOSING SECTION "What I could not verify": name what you could not reach and why; if you believe the space is covered, show the search. An empty section with no reasoning is a failed brief.

Be concrete and concise. No long code dumps.

Use when initializing shadcn, adding components, composing product UI, building custom registries, configuring themes, or troubleshooting component issues.
- vercel:turbopack: Turbopack expert guidance. Use when configuring the Next.js bundler, optimizing HMR, debugging build issues, or understanding the Turbopack vs Webpack differences.
- vercel:vercel-agent: Vercel Agent guidance — AI-powered code review, incident investigation, and SDK installation. Automates PR analysis and anomaly debugging. Use when configuring or understanding Vercel's AI development tools.
- vercel:vercel-cli: Vercel CLI expert guidance. Use when deploying, managing environment variables, linking projects, viewing logs, querying metrics, managing domains, or interacting with the Vercel platform from the command line.
- vercel:vercel-connect: Vercel Connect expert guidance — securely obtain scoped OAuth tokens for third-party services (Slack, GitHub, MCP servers, OAuth, Snowflake) on behalf of apps or users via Vercel OIDC. Use when wiring up third-party API access, connecting to MCP servers, sending Slack messages, accessing GitHub APIs, receiving webhook events from Slack/Linear/GitHub and forwarding them to your agents and apps, or building Eve agent connections.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.

diff --git a/scripts/hooks/pre-commit b/scripts/hooks/pre-commit
index 3b3b270..ec095e6 100755
--- a/scripts/hooks/pre-commit
+++ b/scripts/hooks/pre-commit
@@ -321,4 +321,32 @@ if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
   fi
 fi
 
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# 5. Scoped Vitest — run only the tests related to what's actually staged,
+#    not the whole suite. `vitest related` walks the module graph from the
+#    given files and runs whatever test files transitively depend on them
+#    (or, for a staged *.test.ts(x) itself, just that file). Confirmed
+#    live (2026-08-26): `vitest related` defaults to watch mode and hangs
+#    forever without --run — that flag is not optional here.
+#    Blocks the commit on a real test failure; the full unscoped suite
+#    still runs (and blocks the PR) in CI regardless of what this catches.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+vitest_files=()
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+  [[ -z "$f" ]] && continue
+  vitest_files+=("$f")
+done < <(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR | grep -E '^overrides/.*\.(ts|tsx)$' || true)
+
+if [ "${#vitest_files[@]}" -gt 0 ] && command -v node &>/dev/null; then
+  echo "Running Vitest for files related to your staged changes..."
+  if ! npx vitest related --run "${vitest_files[@]}"; then
+    echo ""
+    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — a related Vitest test failed."
+    echo "      Fix the failure above, then re-stage and commit again."
+    echo ""
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+
 exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Sync .cursor/rules/, .github/copilot-instructions.md, and .vscode/instructions/
 * from .claude/ + AGENTS.md sources.
 *
 * .claude/ + AGENTS.md is the master — never edit derived files that have a
 * synced-from header directly.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs          # report drift
 *   node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --check  # exit 1 if any drift found (CI mode)
 *   node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix    # regenerate auto-generated rules
 */

import fs from 'fs'
import path from 'path'
import {fileURLToPath} from 'url'

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..')

const SQUAD_A_GLOBS = [
    'overrides/app/pages/cart/**',
    'overrides/app/pages/checkout/**',
    'overrides/app/pages/checkout-one-click/**',
    'overrides/app/pages/confirmation/**',
    'overrides/app/components/sf-payments-express/**',
    'overrides/app/components/sf-payments-express-buttons/**',
    'overrides/app/components/multiship/**',
    'overrides/app/components/bonus-product-view-modal/**'
].join(',')

const SQUAD_B_GLOBS = [
    'overrides/app/pages/home/**',
    'overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**',
    'overrides/app/pages/product-list/**',
    'overrides/app/pages/search/**',
    'overrides/app/pages/account/**',
    'overrides/app/pages/store-locator/**',
    'overrides/app/components/search/**',
    'overrides/app/components/store-locator/**'
].join(',')

/**
 * MANIFEST — defines the sync relationship between .claude/ sources and derived targets.
 *
 * All entries are `type: 'auto'` — `--fix` regenerates every target. Three generation modes:

+carries two-to-four Gherkin tags — that's the naming convention doing `@p0`'s job, not a
+dropped tag.

 */

 *This document is for documenting what has been learned - What worked, what failed, what NOT to do again.*
 
+## SFCC-751 QA automation pipeline (2026-08-24/25)
+
+- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
+  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
+  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
+  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
+  runs its tests."
+- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
+  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
+  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
+  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
+  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
+- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
+  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
+  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
+  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
+  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
+  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
+  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
+  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
+  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
+  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
+  skipped) regardless of its title.
+- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
+  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
+  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
+- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
+  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
+  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
+- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
+  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
+  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
+  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for
+  `state: 'hidden'` after the click, not just for the click to register.
+

 *This document is for documenting what has been learned - What worked, what failed, what NOT to do again.*
 
+## SFCC-751 QA automation pipeline (2026-08-24/25)
+
+- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
+  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
+  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
+  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
+  runs its tests."
+- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
+  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
+  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
+  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
+  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
+- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
+  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
+  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
+  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
+  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
+  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
+  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
+  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
+  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
+  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
+  skipped) regardless of its title.
+- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
+  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
+  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
+- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
+  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
+  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
+- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
+  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
+  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
+  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for
+  `state: 'hidden'` after the click, not just for the click to register.

# targeted PR, e2e-localhost only runs the tests tagged for an area
      # (Playwright `{tag: '@<area>'}`, matching the Gherkin `@area` tag
      # documented in e2e/features/README.md) when EVERY changed path that
      # matters to E2E (the `e2e` group above) also falls inside that area's
      # own allow-list — see "Compute E2E scope" below for the subset check.
      # Anything outside every area's allow-list — a shared/global-impact
      # path (Global Shell, theme, hooks, config/, shared E2E infra — see
      # .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md and protectedFiles.md) or simply a path
      # no area has claimed yet — falls back to the full suite by
      # construction, deliberately, rather than needing its own deny-list to
      # maintain. Adding a new area: give it its own allow-list group here,
      # add the matching `@area` Playwright tag to its specs, and see
      # testing.md > Layer 3.
      - name: Get changed files
        id: changed
--- e2e/features/README.md 128-146 at head ---
## CI gates

| Trigger | What runs | Environment |
|---|---|---|
| PR → `develop` | Change-scoped — only the `@area` tag(s) touched by the diff (falls back to the full suite for a shared/global-impact path, or any path no area has claimed) — desktop Chromium + mobile Chrome | `npm start` on localhost, SFCC dev API |
| PR → `develop`, Jira key referenced | BrowserStack, scoped to that story's `@SFCC-NNN` tag(s) only. No key referenced in the PR title/body/branch → BrowserStack doesn't run at all | SFCC SIT environment |
| PR → `release/**` | Full suite, unscoped — desktop Chromium + mobile Chrome | `npm start` on localhost, SFCC dev API |
| PR → `release/**` | Full suite on BrowserStack (Chrome, Safari, Firefox), unscoped — a release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply here | SFCC SIT environment |
| Push/PR on `release/**` | P0 suite only (`*.p0.spec.ts`) via Digital SIT gate | SFCC SIT environment |

Change-scoping mechanics (which paths map to which `@area`, and the exact narrowing rule) live
in `.github/workflows/qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` job — see
[.claude/rules/testing.md > Change-scoped E2E](../../.claude/rules/testing.md#change-scoped-e2e-develop-targeted-prs-only).
Every spec's Playwright tag must match its `.feature` file's `@area` tag above, or it only ever
runs via the full-suite fallback.

BrowserStack story-scoping mechanics (Jira key detection, `--grep` scoping, the release-always-
full-suite exception) live in
[.claude/rules/testing.md > BrowserStack story scoping](../../.claude/rules/testing.md#browserstack-story-scoping).

I have everything I need. Writing up.

## R2 — Conventions, Tier & Ownership: review of PR #61

Rubric read at base `8362b3c` throughout. Head is `74e2b82`.

---

### 1. Tier & ownership classification — all 42 paths

**Tier 1 (12 paths, `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` via base `CODEOWNERS`):**
`.browserstack.yml` (D, CODEOWNERS:60 / frozenFiles.md:114) · `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` · `.claude/rules/testing.md` · `CODEOWNERS` · `package.json` · `vitest.config.ts` · `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` · `.github/workflows/{deploy-preview,e2e-browserstack-preview,protected-file-guard,qa,zephyr-results-sync}.yml`

**Tier 2: zero.** No `overrides/`, no `theme/components/`, no `translations/`, no `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, no `scripts/contentful/`.

**Untiered but owned (9 paths, `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-qa-team` via `CODEOWNERS:e2e/`):** all 9 `e2e/**` files.

**UNOWNED AND UNTIERED — 21 of 42 (50%).** CONFIRMED / DEFECT. No base `CODEOWNERS` pattern matches, and no tier in base `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md`:
`.claude/skills/project-init/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md`, `.cursor/rules/testing.mdc`, `.cursor/rules/tier1FrozenFiles.mdc`, `.cursor/rules/skills/{project-init,qa-generate}.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.vscode/instructions/workflows.md`, `.docs/architecture.md`, `.docs/memory/feedback.md`, `.docs/memory/projectState.md`, `.docs/prompts/qaClaudeCodeSetup.md`, `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-claude-code-brief.md`, `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md`, `.env.sample`, `.gitignore`, `browserstack.yml`, `package-lock.json`, `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs`, `scripts/projectInitCheck.sh`, `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs`.

Three of these are structurally significant, not incidental:

- **DEFECT (pre-existing, but this PR is the first to exercise it): the Tier 1 governance mirrors are unowned.** `.claude/rules/` is Tier 1; its generated mirrors `.cursor/rules/tier1FrozenFiles.mdc` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (which carry the *same* frozen-file list verbatim) match no CODEOWNERS pattern — `CODEOWNERS` scopes `.github/workflows/` only, not `.github/**`. **Decoy:** hand-edit `.cursor/rules/tier1FrozenFiles.mdc` to delete a frozen path, staging no `.claude/` source. `scripts/hooks/pre-commit:76` only runs the sync when a `.claude/rules/**` or `SKILL.md` is staged, so it never fires; `protected-file-guard.yml`'s tier1 `files_yaml` (head lines 96–133) has no `.cursor`/`.vscode` entry; `sync:ai-rules:check` appears in **no** workflow (search scope: `git grep "sync:ai-rules\|syncCursorRules" -- .github/` at both `8362b3c` and `pr/61` — only `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:54` and the file's own header comment). That decoy merges green with zero Tier 1 review.
- **DEFECT: `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` and `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` are unowned credential handlers.** Both construct Basic-auth headers from `JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN` and BrowserStack keys (`zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:98-99`), and the sync script runs in a `workflow_run` context that carries real secrets. `CODEOWNERS` covers `scripts/hooks/`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/contentful/**` — there is no catch-all for `scripts/`.
- **NOTE: `package-lock.json` is tier-mismatched.** It *is* in `protected-file-guard.yml`'s tier1 pattern list (head:112) but is in neither base `frozenFiles.md` nor base `CODEOWNERS` — so it triggers the warning but is not code-owner-gated. Pre-existing.

---

### 2. AGENTS.md Hard Rules

- **HR4 — CLEAN, verified.** None of `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` appears in `git diff --name-status 8362b3c pr/61`. The absolute set is untouched.
- **HR8 — CONFIRMED / BLOCKER.** `vitest.config.ts:13-30` adds a `coverage` block. `playwright.config.js` and `.storybook/` are **not** touched (verified against the name-status list) — `vitest.config.ts` is the sole HR8 file. The only stated justification is a source comment: *"added at the developer's explicit request for whole-tree visibility"* (`vitest.config.ts:18-19`). A comment written by the change's author is not owner approval. The PR body does not mention `vitest.config.ts` at all.
- **HR7 — CONFIRMED / BLOCKER.** `package.json:31` adds `@vitest/coverage-v8` ^3.2.7 (+237 lines of lock). I read the full PR body via `gh pr view 61 --json body` and all 20 commit bodies: no integration-team approval anywhere. Commit `74e2b82` explains the version pin only.
- **HR2 — CONFIRMED / BLOCKER.** 12 Tier 1 paths, none named as Tier 1 in the PR body, no approval recorded. Whether the verified-session exception applies turns on TimLavelleACC's team membership, which I cannot check (see §8).
- **HR9 — DEFECT.** `.browserstack.yml` is deleted. Setting aside the tier question the lead settled, **the PR body never mentions the rename at all** — it describes only a `projectName` correction. A Tier 1 file deletion is undisclosed to the reviewer.
- **HR10 — CONFIRMED / DEFECT.** Tier 1 + QA-owned + 21 unowned paths in one change, no scope-confirmation statement.
- **HR12 — DEFECT.** `e2e/fixtures/products.js:8-31` ships provisional regional prices while its own comment records an unresolved question ("*Whether the numeric values need to change… is a real open question for the integration team*"). The rule is stop-and-ask, not ship-and-annotate. This change is also outside SFCC-751 — the comment concedes no spec exists that would hit it.
- **HR14 — NOTE.** Disposition recorded in `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:11-14` ("Sprint: N/A"). `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` at base is stale ("Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress)", dated 2026-06-23), so it can't adjudicate this. Pre-existing.

---

### 3. Derived-config mirror integrity — CLEAN, mechanically proved

I extracted `pr/61` to a scratch tree, forced mtimes so the mtime-gated sync would actually run, and executed `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix` (the script is unmodified by this PR). All 23 targets regenerated; `diff -r` against the committed versions is **byte-identical** for `.cursor/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and `.vscode/instructions/workflows.md`. No hand-editing, no drift. CONFIRMED.

**But the check that would have caught it is a decoy.** `syncCursorRules.mjs:286-330` compares `mtime` only, never content. On a fresh clone or CI checkout all mtimes are equal, so `--check` reports "in sync" for a hand-edited target. My first run proved this: it printed *"All targets are in sync"* without regenerating anything. Combined with §1's finding that `--check` runs in no workflow, the mirror integrity of Tier 1 governance content rests entirely on a bypassable local hook. NOTE (pre-existing), but load-bearing for the unowned-mirror DEFECT above.

---

### 4. `.docs/temp/` working docs — should not ship as-is. DEFECT.

- **Precedent cuts against them.** `.docs/temp/` at base holds exactly two files, `openItems.md` and `tsd-architecture.md` — durable project docs. Meanwhile base `.gitignore:58,60` explicitly ignores two *ephemeral* things inside that same folder (`xlsxSnapshot/`, `integrationReviewSnapshot`). The established convention is: durable content tracked, working artifacts ignored. These two are working artifacts. (Search scope: `git log --all -- .docs/temp` and `git ls-tree -r 8362b3c -- .docs/temp`.)
- **One of them is explicitly known-wrong.** `SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:3-6` says the brief is superseded and *"do not follow its Deliverable 1 target."* Committing a superseded AI brief as a tracked file guarantees a future reader follows the wrong one.
- **They are now load-bearing from production source.** `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:15` and `.github/workflows/zephyr-results-sync.yml:11` both cite `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md`. Either it is durable documentation (then it belongs outside `temp/`) or it is scratch (then shipped code must not cite it). It cannot be both.
- **It contains a fabricated ownership fact.** `SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:15` states `.github/workflows/` is *"Tier 1 (CODEOWNERS → @hsemp)"*. `@hsemp` appears **nowhere** at base (search scope: `git grep -l "hsemp" 8362b3c` over the entire tree — no match); at head it exists only in this one file. Base `CODEOWNERS:70` routes that path to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, and the file's own header states individual usernames were removed from Tier 1.
- `SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:215` is a literal Claude Code session prompt. Session scaffolding, not project documentation.

---

### 5. E2E conventions and POM audit

**Filename convention — CONFIRMED / DEFECT.** Base `.claude/rules/testing.md` specifies `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`; the Jira ticket independently specifies `{JIRA-KEY}-{description}.{priority}.spec.ts`. Both delivered specs are `…spec.js` with **no priority segment** — `SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js`, `SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`. The priority is carried as a `@p1` Playwright tag instead, which the PR's own `e2e/features/README.md:44-49` edit says is *not* how priority is expressed. `@p1` is also absent from that file's tag table.

*Countervailing, worth stating:* Tier 1 `playwright.config.js:18` sets `testMatch: '**/*.spec.js'` globally; only the `p0` project (line 54) accepts `.ts`. A non-p0 `.spec.ts` would be collected by **no** project. So `.js` is the working choice and testing.md's documented `.spec.ts` convention is currently unrunnable — a pre-existing rule/config contradiction this PR neither fixes nor flags, while editing testing.md heavily. NOTE.

**Gherkin-first — DEFECT.** A `.feature` exists for the desktop spec. **None exists for `SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`** (`e2e/features/` at head contains only `SMOKE-homepage-load.feature` and `SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.feature`). Base testing.md: *"no Playwright code is written until sign-off."* No Lead-QA sign-off evidence appears in the PR body, commits, or `.docs/`.

**A deliberately red test is being merged — BLOCKER.** `SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js:36-40`: *"Expected to fail today: the mobile drawer currently has no category navigation content at all."* It is a plain `test()`, not `test.fixme()`. `.docs/memory/projectState.md:78-81` confirms this is intentional. Once merged it sits in `e2e/tests/zimm` and will fail in every full-suite run (`release/**` PRs, `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` on release, `digital-sit.yml` if it ever gets a `.p0.` name). Playwright provides `test.fixme()` for exactly this; using it preserves the visibility the comment wants without a permanently red gate.

**POM selector priority — DEFECT, and a regression in a shared file.**
- `e2e/support/pages/BasePage.js:117` replaces the tier-1 accessible selector `getByRole('button', {name: /decline tracking/i})` with `dialog.locator('.chakra-modal__body button:visible')` — a **class-name selector**, which base testing.md's Page Object Model section explicitly forbids ("Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position").
